readerContract.humanQuestion: What did Trump actually say in the September 14 AI posts, and did the statement change rules or tools?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Understand the reported claim and its stated qualification while separating a sharper public position from a rule change.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: A reader may see a viral post about AI risk and assume her AI tools or the law changed that day.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A political post states a view about oversight. A government action names the mechanism that changes duties or powers; the report identifies no such action here, while the administration says it wants smart regulation.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: When a political AI headline travels through group chats or a workplace conversation, a reader can ask what was said, what instrument followed, and whether anything actually changed.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A short September 14 NewsStand follow-up on reported social-media posts, not a legal survey or a replay of yesterday’s story.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can explain why this is a new escalation in the public argument without telling people a rule exists when it does not.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Trump said a strong president, rather than additional limits, was the control AI needed; AP also reported the administration said it was concerned about AI and wanted smart regulation. Neither statement is a reported new rule.
causalSequence: Trump’s posts reject AI-risk warnings and say a strong president is the necessary control.
The administration’s stated qualification is that it is concerned about AI and wants smart regulation.
Neither statement names an enacted action that changes duties or a product setting; AP reports no such action here.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A colleague sends the post and asks whether it means ChatGPT or another AI tool is now less regulated. The answer is no: the reported event is a position, not a reported product or rule change.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: For another policy headline, ask whether it names the action, who carries it out and which people or products it actually covers.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Before sharing a claim about AI guardrails, ask: what changed on paper or in the product after the statement?
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Treat this as a narrow dated follow-up. Do not repeat the September 13 remarks, predict policy, or imply a tool setting changed.
